newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end touch firmer, Olivetti falls.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end touch firmer, Olivetti falls.

text.p: Italian shares closed slightly higher on Thursday helped by Wall Street's firm opening on lower than expected U.S. PPI data, but trading remained thin and technical, traders said.

Troubled high-tech group Olivetti turned down by close, off 1.58 percent at 574 lire on volume of over 40 million shares, after managing to stay firm all morning. Olivetti managers and auditors were currently meeting bourse watchdog Consob on group accounts. "The stock is still very fragile," one dealer said.
The All-share Mibtel index ended 0.37 percent up at 9,438 and the Mib30 blue chip index closed up 0.5 percent at 14,050.

Parmalat, Italy's largest listed food group, saw a session of see-sawing movement, its image affected by a botulism scare linked to mascarpone cream cheese. Having gained some four percent in the morning it closed 4.4 percent down at 1,802.
In blue chips, energy giant Eni put on 1.11 percent to 6,645 lire, tyre and cable maker Pirelli rose 0.93 percent to 2,610 and Telecom Italia gained 0.61 percent to 2,965.

But mobile phone operator TIM slipped 0.2 percent to 3,035 lire on news the government approved a bill setting out tender details for Italy's third mobile phone operating licence, expected to be awarded by the end of 1996 or start of 1997.

Fiat continued weak, hit by worries over the depressed new car market in Italy and on news the carmaker said it intends to substantially boost investment in Poland, traders said. The stock closed 0.82 percent down at 4,345 after touching a low of 4,280 lire, around nearly three-year lows.
Banks were mixed but insurers were generally firm with Generali up 1.51 percent at 33,864 following news of a 1-for-10 scrip issue.
